reason: Chalice CLI quickstart can create a project and serve it locally with `chalice local` on CPU without AWS credentials.
demo: README Quickstart: chalice new-project, then run the app locally with chalice local
goal: Install chalice from the repo clone and make the quickstart work offline: `chalice new-project helloworld` then `chalice local --port 8000` inside that project (no AWS deploy, no credentials). Write /work/run.sh so it creates the project at /work/helloworld (if missing), starts `chalice local --port 8000` in the background (nohup), and waits until http://127.0.0.1:8000/ responds. Write /work/env.sh to activate the environment where chalice is installed.
check: A fresh new-project is scaffolded in a temp dir, and the local server on port 8000 returns HTTP 200 with the JSON {"hello": "world"} for GET /.
